component.name: Almanac
component.summary: See everything installed, where it came from, and what needs you

description.p: Almanac is a catalogue of everything installed on this machine: packages from the repositories and the AUR, Flatpaks, AppImages, local git checkouts, Omarchy plugins and themes, and the AI agent tooling no package manager tracks.

It is opinionated about provenance. Before you install anything from a marketplace, Almanac shows the repository the code actually comes from — which is not the same as the author name in its manifest — and whether what you are about to install is still the commit that was reviewed.
What it covers:

ul.li: One update list across six package managers, with versions-behind counts
An app store over the Omarchy plugin marketplace, Omarchy themes and ArtCraft
Agent CLIs, MCP servers, skills, plugins and hooks, with live health
System health checks that each offer the one command that acts on them
Install and removal inside the app, always showing the full list first

screenshot.caption: Plugins, apps and themes with provenance on every card
Themes previewed in their own colours
One update list for six package managers
Agent CLIs, MCP servers, skills and hooks
System health, each check with the command that acts on it

description.p: Choose when the scheduled update runs, and let it update Almanac.

ul.li: Preferences, Updates: pick the day and the time the scheduled update runs, as well as how often.

A new "Almanac itself" switch lets the scheduled update install a newer Almanac release, checked against its published checksums. It is off by default; left off, the run tells you a new release is out.

description.p: Almanac can update itself when installed from the package on its GitHub releases page.

ul.li: A newer release shows in Updates and is part of Update all.
The package is downloaded for that exact version, checked against the checksums published with it, and installed with pacman -U after asking for your password.

description.p: Arch news, a checked Update all, a scheduled update in the package, and a History page that shows what each action did.

ul.li: Arch news appears in the app. Update all asks about unread posts first, and the scheduled update holds while one is unread.
After Update all, Almanac checks what changed: what is still waiting, services that failed, programs that need a rebuild, and a restart the new kernel needs. It offers to repair what it can.
The scheduled update ships in the package. It fails safe when it cannot tell what is pending, and leaves AUR packages to a person.
History opens each action to what it did. Almanac's own log expires after 30 days and can be cleared.
Health checks run side by side, each with a time limit. A check that could not run says so instead of passing, and a fix that could not be checked is not called resolved.
Health stays on the disk it starts on, so network mounts are not walked.
The Close button on task dialogs works again.
The package cache estimate no longer counts anything twice.
Starting up and scanning are faster, and the catalogue takes less memory.
Every page shares one layout, and severity labels line up.
Demo mode changes nothing on the machine.
The desktop file is named after the app id.

description.p: Fixes from a full audit of the app.

ul.li: "Update all" no longer reports every update installed when the check for updates itself failed, for example offline.
Trimming the package cache now keeps two versions of installed packages as it says; before, it only cleared uninstalled ones.
Clearing old session logs no longer removes the running shell's socket after a few days of uptime.
Removing an AppImage from its row menu asks first.
The header button always names what it does on the page shown.
Commands that run as root are named by full path, never found through a PATH that user-writable folders come first in.
Settings, caches and history are written so that two writers or a crash can no longer leave a broken file.
Switching on a startup app the system ships switched off now works.
Scheduled updates hold back a kernel when the list of pending updates cannot be read, instead of installing it.
Releases come with SHA256SUMS and a signed build provenance.

description.p: Building the package no longer fails now and then on a test that timed how soon GTK frees a closed window. Nothing else changes.
Scheduled updates hold more of what can stop a boot: every kernel flavour, CPU microcode, DKMS modules, the NVIDIA driver, and what builds the initramfs or unlocks the root disk.

Plugin setup runs exactly the words you saw, checks every shown file is unchanged before each step, and no longer offers steps that run a program instead of setting one up, or that point a tool at files it could not show. Errors read as plain English, and deeply nested data can no longer crash the window.

Safer scheduled updates: when Almanac cannot tell which pending updates touch boot, the update is held instead of applied, and AUR updates are checked too. AppImages built for another processor are refused, a download without a published checksum says so, and an update that worked is no longer reported as failed.

Plugin trust is tied to where the code comes from: a plugin is Verified only when it is the listed repository at the reviewed commit, setup shows every file a step runs, and your GitHub token is sent only to GitHub's API. Switches no longer flip back on their own after a failed change, plugin toggles cannot hang, and adding an AppImage no longer freezes the window.

Safer AppImage updates: a download that is cut short, is not an app, or does not match GitHub's checksum is discarded, and the working copy and its backup are left alone. The App Store runs only the install commands its catalogue uses, and plugin setup shows the whole script before it runs.

Faster: startup launches about a quarter as many programs, slow checks no longer freeze the window, and MCP servers are no longer started just to list them. Closed task windows are freed, old cache files are pruned, and a package install says when a newer release is out.
Fixed: Update all left plugins, AppImages, agent CLIs and local checkouts listed after it ran, because it only ran the system update. It now updates everything it counts, each with its own updater.
Each release now comes with a ready-to-install package.
Fixed: building the package without a display (a clean chroot) crashed in its tests. CI now runs the tests that way too.
Updates and History explain themselves.

ul.li: When the update count jumps, the Updates page says why: on Omarchy, a new batch of Arch packages from the stable mirror, with the dates of the batch you have and the batch on offer
The Updates page says when the pending batch needs a restart, and names the packages that do (the kernel, systemd, glibc, graphics drivers, firmware)
History opens with one line for the last 24 hours, and the weekly scheduled update now records what it updated
Fixed: dependencies with version constraints, links with query strings and names with an ampersand blanked their row or notification

description.p: Almanac is now written in Rust.

ul.li: The same app, ported line for line: every page, dialog, action and command-line option, with settings, history and caches from 1.x carried over untouched
Held to the Python original by a parity check that runs both on the same inputs, and by the Python's whole test suite, ported
Fixed: a late icon download could land on a different row of a list that had been scrolled
Vendor logos from sites that refuse a TLS handshake without post-handshake authentication now load

description.p: Today's picks, and text you can read on any theme.

ul.li: Today's picks: the app and plugin of the day, ranked on stars and forks in the last 24 hours, downloads and comments this week, each figure labelled with exactly what it counts
Text contrast is measured against the active theme: 7:1 for primary text, 5.5:1 for secondary and accent text
Status pills are solid, with whichever text reads best on each
New Privacy switch for the GitHub figures behind Today's picks

description.p: A denser, calmer window, and Featured is now Today.

ul.li: Every page fits more: compact sidebar, one-line rows, explanations in tooltips, and passing health checks folded into one row
Three App Store cards across, with nothing truncated
The Switchboard leaves plugins to the Plugins page

description.p: A Switchboard for everything with an on/off, proper Preferences, and notifications when plugin updates are waiting.

ul.li: Switchboard: plugins, startup apps, background services and Almanac's own background work, each with a switch
Preferences in four pages, with a switch for everything Almanac fetches over the network
The settings watcher notifies you when new plugin updates are available
Fixed: closing the settings could save the plugin update scope as the update schedule

description.p: A Plugins page: every plugin on the system, with a switch, a logo, and what state it is in.

ul.li: Switch any plugin on or off, built-in or your own
Plugins are classified before updating; a development link is never updated
Update every plugin at once, within a trust scope you choose
Keyboard shortcuts for a plugin's panel, checked for conflicts
Restart the shell, clearing its compiled cache

description.p: Over a thousand plugins that used to say "Manual setup" install in one click, and Almanac walks you through the setup their README asks for.

ul.li: Packages a plugin needs are installed for you, with a snapshot first and the result checked
Build steps and setup scripts are shown in full, then run in a terminal you can watch
Credentials and config edits are listed with the README section to read

description.p: Known vulnerabilities from the Arch Security Tracker, a history of what changed on this machine, and a settings watcher that works while Almanac is closed.

ul.li: Security updates are the ones that fix a known vulnerability in the installed version, not a guess from the package name
History: package changes, snapshots, settings resets and Almanac's own actions on one timeline, by day
An optional background watcher notices settings reset to their defaults while the window is closed
Every icon-only control is named for screen readers, and status colours meet WCAG AA in light and dark themes
The interface is translatable, through GNU gettext

description.p: Almanac now checks that what it did actually happened, and watches for changes made behind your back.

ul.li: Every update, install and cleanup reports what changed, not whether a command exited successfully
Settings reset to their defaults are detected and restored in one click
Packages are snapshotted before they change, on systems with Snapper
File types an install took over can be handed back
Install any GitHub project from its link, with every way it ships compared and the download checksum-verified
Major releases wait for you; local changes to plugins are carried forward or set aside, never discarded

description.p: Apps whose release could not be looked up are listed as not checked, and retried within minutes, instead of being shown as having no Linux build.
Health check cleanups that cannot free anything no longer stay listed: the package cache is rated by what a trim would free, and the journal vacuum runs with the permission it needs.
Updates you have already installed no longer stay in the updates list, and a repository update that needs a full upgrade says so instead of silently doing nothing.
First release.
